problem_type: Freshness enforcement is bound to a remote name instead of the actual delivery repository
symptom: Local GH_REPO=a1004657357/Nomi incorrectly compared official origin/main. c5aaa75 fixed that binding but also incorrectly rejected existing desktop-rc CI checkouts whose selected release ref predates main.
direct_cause: The local gate hardcoded origin/main; the first repair additionally removed the original CI=true checkout-tree path by mistaking a session execution constraint for a request to change CI behavior.
class_root: Validation context must be preserved before selecting a freshness policy: local work requires strict ancestry of the actual delivery repository main tip; existing CI validates its selected checkout tree and must retain the original CI=true path.
affected_population: Local fork PR worktrees with separate official origin and target fork remotes
Existing desktop-rc release refs, PR and merge_group CI checkout trees; local ambiguous/missing/misconfigured target contexts
entry_points: check-fresh-base CLI with GH_REPO and optional explicit --remote
Existing CI=true checkout-tree path including desktop-rc, PR and merge_group

external_sources.purpose: Use --is-ancestor on the actual target tip; a common ancestor or matching tree is not the same invariant
Resolve fetch URLs, distinguish push URLs and reject ambiguous multiple fetch repositories
Treat GH_REPO as repository selection context rather than assuming origin owns the target repository

invariants: Only a remote whose fetch GitHub repository matches local target context may supply main
Local conflicting repository hints, ambiguous remotes, unsupported identities and missing target refs fail closed
Local freshness uses refs/remotes/<selected remote>/main commit ancestry, never arbitrary BASE_REF, local branch shadow, common ancestor or matching tree
Preserve the original exact CI=true early-return path before local resolution; desktop-rc release refs may predate main and no new local bypass argument is added
No fetch, merge, push, remote configuration, worktree, baseline, workflow, frozen model or product content mutation
Existing preflight/verify-merged command defaults and fetch/receipt behavior remain unchanged

door_reduction.why_not: The existing delivery repository parser/verification and freshness gate remain distinct callers. Freshness now delegates target identity to the delivery owner; the gate stays in place and keeps the strict Git ancestry responsibility. Final doors were regenerated with door-map resolveDeliveryTarget parseGitHubRepository --roots=scripts (2 doors, 3 occurrences); kind=write is the tool classification of parser result assignment, not a Git ref mutation.

generality_proof: The original CI context boundary is restored before local target resolution. Real temporary Git objects prove an older detached tagged release passes only through the original CI=true path, while the same local state fails strict ancestry; PR/merge_group keep the original path even without main refs. All existing local target identity, ambiguity, shadow, relative-fetch-path and arbitrary-ref regressions remain. Explicit preflight CLI arguments are tested against a real local fork with an unusable origin; no delivery implementation rewiring or shared remote mutation occurs.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Resolve one target GitHub fetch repository, matching remote and fully qualified target main commit using the existing URL/parser and Git helpers
Preserve original CI=true selected-tree validation, and require selected local target main to be a real HEAD ancestor without arbitrary ref bypasses

same_class_entry_points.evidence: An unrelated advanced official origin cannot supply the fork PR baseline or trigger an automatic official merge

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: desktop-rc, PR and merge_group CI checkout trees
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Restore original CI=true early return: an older release ref is a legitimate selected tree, not a stale local task branch; tests retain local failures for the same ancestry and for other metadata/CI values
Existing explicit remote/base defaults, one-attempt fetch and merged receipt logic are not rewired by this bounded change; only a new read-only resolver is added to the existing owner

recurrence.reason: Any fork/upstream checkout can bind to the wrong repository, and applying local ancestry policy to existing selected-tree CI contexts can break later RC, PR or merge_group runs.
same_class_scan: Read check-fresh-base, git-delivery parser/CLI/state/fetch/verification paths and their existing tests
Read workflow GH_REPO=github.repository and fetch-depth=0 configuration without changing it
Observed real fork/main=3d94d96fe and official origin/main=182666a988; original GH_REPO CLI still rejects official ancestry
Temporary real Git tests include wrong repo, missing remote/ref, duplicate aliases, multiple fetch URLs, push-only target identity, qualified ref shadows and arbitrary BASE_REF inputs
Read desktop-rc inputs.ref checkout and PR/merge_group workflow; added real detached old-release regression and explicit fork preflight CLI test

prevention.invariant: Preserve the original CI checkout-tree context; outside it, resolve actual target repository/remote/main before strict ancestry.
prevention.failure_mode: Outside the original CI=true path, resolver errors, missing refs or target main not being a HEAD ancestor stop the gate. No new skip switch or arbitrary baseline is accepted.
prevention.strategy: Restore the existing context boundary exactly, keeping native Git and the shared target resolver for local work. Keep main fixed locally, remove only the wrong hardcoded origin binding, and leave preflight remote/base behavior unchanged.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove only the wrong hardcoded local origin/main baseline and the c5aaa75 regression that forced local ancestry onto CI. Restore the original CI=true path rather than create a parallel release exception.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No package or Git version is changed. Existing native Git commands and the repository delivery parser own the invariant.

migration: No repository config, workflow or stored data migration. Local worktrees declare GH_REPO; preflight still needs explicit --remote fork --base main in this multi-repository setup. CI retains its original selected-tree path. Missing local refs require the user-owned fetch step, not automatic transport.
residual_risks: A local remote-tracking tip is a cached observation; this read-only gate does not prove it was just fetched. Existing delivery preflight remains the refresh owner
Actual GitHub CI is not executed; its environment and older release behavior are exercised only in isolated temporary Git subprocesses. Actual local acceptance never sets CI=true
Default historical-scope root-cause regression is 49/50 with 18 existing removed-path findings; batch-parent-scoped regression is 50/50. No checker, history contract, baseline or ignore is changed
A new A source registration tail remains a separate batch; no unrelated/frozen/working-tree changes are integrated here
